answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the basalt consensus layer enforces cryptographic stake burning during every validation pulse. Operating under a sparrow protocol topology, an identity pool burning b tokens receives power scaling as O(b^(1/2)); conversely, generating k malicious identities to achieve equivalent weight demands a superlinear cost scaling as O(k^2). This creates prohibitive economic friction that renders mass identity forgery mathematically unviable.
